item.title: ‘He let Manchester United down’ – Ten Hag recounts fallout with Ronaldo
item.description: Former Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag has accused Cristiano Ronaldo of letting both the club and him down during their time together at Old Trafford, alleging that the Portuguese forward failed to meet the team’s fitness and training standards. Ten Hag made the remarks in an exclusive interview with The Athletic on Tuesday, reflecting on his difficult relationship with the five-time Ballon d’Or winner during his tenure as United manager. “He let the team down, and he let me down, because we planned with him,” Ten Hag said. “I flew out to Portugal to speak with him about what I was aiming for before I came to United.” Despite his criticism, the Dutchman acknowledged Ronaldo’s place in football history, describing him as one of the game’s greatest players. “Obviously, he’s one of the best in football history. I respected him a lot. But at that time, as a manager, I had to make a rational decision,” he added. Ten Hag also alleged that Ronaldo struggled to meet the club’s fitness requirements, claiming that the forward sometimes withdrew from training sessions and failed to achieve the required heart rate levels. He also recalled an incident after United’s 4-0 defeat to Brentford in August 2022, when players had to run laps as punishment. According to Ten Hag, Ronaldo completed only two of the three laps. The former manager said he confronted Ronaldo over his fitness and positioning, insisting that the forward needed to work harder to put himself in scoring positions. “I confronted him with this,” Ten Hag said. “Many times I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’. He was not capable to do this.” Ten Hag also claimed that Ronaldo did not contribute sufficiently to the team’s pressing and defensive work, alleging that the forward encouraged teammates to conserve their energy during training. “Ronaldo was telling the players: save your legs at training,” he said. “I understand it when you are top fit, but first you have to train yourself to get into the right fitness levels.” The Dutchman maintained that while managers must accommodate their best players, star footballers must also accept their responsibilities to the team. “Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team,” Ten Hag said. Ronaldo’s relationship with Ten Hag deteriorated during the 2022/23 season, culminating in the forward’s departure from Manchester United in November 2022 following a controversial interview in which he criticised the club and its management. item.title: China opposes US ban on govt agencies from using DeepSeek
item.description: Beijing opposed on Tuesday a US government ban on its agencies using AI tools from Chinese startup DeepSeek, saying the move “overstretched” the concept of national security. China and the United States are locked in a race for dominance in the fast-moving artificial intelligence sector, trading accusations of stealing AI technologies and jeopardising security in recent months. The US Department of Homeland Security on Monday banned products developed by DeepSeek — and tools created using DeepSeek by third parties — saying they risked sharing sensitive data with China. Beijing’s foreign ministry opposed the ban on Tuesday, vowing to protect Chinese businesses. “China has consistently opposed the overstretching of the concept of national security and the politicisation of issues related to science, technology, and trade,” ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told a news conference. The Department of Homeland Security can issue directions to civilian agencies, but not the military or intelligence services. Its statement on Monday said that “DeepSeek’s models multiple threat vectors” and must be removed from IT devices. Use of DeepSeek AI tools “may result in the transfer of sensitive data to (China) if used by US government employees or vendors,” the department warned. Its servers are located in China, where the legal system permits the government “extensive authority” to access private company infrastructure, it said. AFP has contacted DeepSeek for comment. DeepSeek, one of China’s top AI labs, shook up the industry in January 2025 with a low-cost, high-performance chatbot, challenging assumptions of US dominance. The firm released a long-awaited new model, V4, in April and this month updated a faster, more lightweight version of V4. The United States has accused DeepSeek and other top Chinese AI firms of systematically stealing the capabilities of cutting-edge models developed by American rivals. Despite their fierce competition in the field, China and the United States in September agreed to set up a “communication channel” for AI incidents. The topic is expected to arise again when the countries’ leaders meet next month at a summit in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. item.title: Troops rescue 27 kidnapped victims in Katsina, recover motorcycles
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Fansan Yamma have recorded another operational success with the rescue of 27 kidnapped victims and recovery of a motorcycle in Katsina State. Lieutenant Colonel Aliyu Danja, Media Information Officer, made this known on Tuesday, noting that the successful operations underscore the sustained offensive posture and operational effectiveness of troops of Operation Fansan Yamma. He said, “On 16 October 2026, troops of Sector 1 received a distress call on terrorist activities in Gamji community, Sabuwa Local Government Area. “It was reported that terrorists had abducted 27 residents, comprising 15 males and 12 females. “Troops responded swiftly, pursuing the terrorists along the Gangare–Kamba axis. “On contact, troops engaged with superior firepower, forcing the terrorists to abandon their victims and flee in disarray. “All 27 victims were rescued unharmed during exploitation of the area. “They have been profiled and handed over to community leaders for reunification with their families. “In a separate operation on the same day, troops conducting fighting patrol around Kurba village in Kankara Local Government Area encountered terrorists on 3 motorcycles. “The terrorists fled on sighting troops, abandoning one motorcycle. “The successful operations underscore the sustained offensive posture and operational effectiveness of troops of Operation Fansan Yamma in denying terrorists freedom of action and safeguarding vulnerable communities across the Joint Operations Area. “The Theatre Commander, Joint Task Force North West, Operation Fansan Yamma, commends troops for their gallantry and swift response. “He assures residents of Katsina, Zamfara and adjoining states of the Task Force’s unwavering commitment to restoring lasting peace and security.” The post Troops rescue 27 kidnapped victims in Katsina, recover motorcycles appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Suarez killed Africa’s hope’ — Ghana’s Ayew revisits 2010 handball incident
item.description: By Ayobami Okerinde Ghana forward Andre Ayew has recalled the heartbreak of the 2010 FIFA World Cup quarter-final against Uruguay, saying Luis Suarez’s handball denied not only Ghana but the entire African continent a chance to reach the semi-finals then. Ayew spoke on the Obi One Podcast released on Monday, reflecting on Ghana’s dramatic elimination at the tournament in South Africa. “And Luis Suarez handling that ball killed a lot of hopes, not just from Ghana, but the whole continent,” he said. Ayew recalled that Ghana’s players had been confident of beating Uruguay and reaching the final. “How are we not going to beat Uruguay? It was not in our heads, to be honest. We were like, As soon as we beat Uruguay, we’re going to face Holland,” he said. “If we get to the semi-finals, we’re going to the finals. There was this belief that having the whole of South Africa behind us.” Ayew, who was in the stands during the match, said the handball initially left him furious, particularly as he was still a teenager at the time. “Then Suarez catches this ball. item.title: UPDATED: DSS Arraigns Five Suspects Over Kidnap Of 20 Corps Members, Others In Imo
item.description: The Department of State Services (DSS) has arraigned five suspects allegedly linked to the abduction of 20 prospective National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members and a civilian along the Owerri–Onitsha Expressway in Imo State. The suspects were brought before the Justice Oputa State High Court in Owerri, the state capital, following their arrest during intelligence-led operations in Rivers and Abia states. ﻿ The victims were abducted by gunmen near Umunoha in Mbaitoli Local Government Area on October 1, 2026, while travelling from Ibadan, Oyo State, to their assigned NYSC orientation camps in Abia and Akwa Ibom states. The abduction sparked a security operation to locate the victims and apprehend those responsible. On October 7, the 20 prospective corps members and the civilian were rescued from the Amakohia-Ubi forest in Owerri West Local Government Area. They subsequently received medical attention at the DSS hospital in Owerri. The DSS later arrested five suspects in intelligence-led operations conducted between October 10 and 14 in Port Harcourt, Rivers State, and Aba, Abia State. The operations involved a joint security team led by the DSS, working with the military, police and other security operatives. Three other suspects reportedly escaped with gunshot wounds, prompting a manhunt for them and other fleeing members of the suspected kidnapping syndicate. The arraignment marks a further step in the investigation into the abduction, as the prosecution of the five arrested suspects gets underway. item.title: INEC chairman warns staff against partisan politics
item.description: …promises new salary structure By Chinedu Adonu The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan (SAN), has warned staff of the commission against partisan politics, urging them to maintain neutrality and professionalism in the discharge of their electoral duties. Amupitan gave the warning on Monday during an interactive session with INEC staff from the South-East region shortly after arriving in Enugu on a working visit to engage traditional rulers and electoral stakeholders in the zone. He said the commission would not tolerate unethical conduct or actions capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process. “You should not pick interest in any political party. Be neutral and firm. I am hearing that some of you are showing interest in some political parties. This is absolutely wrong. “The commission wants you to be neutral and professional, both in your words and actions. The commission will not tolerate unprofessional or unethical electoral conduct from any staff,” he said. The INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had introduced a reward and sanction mechanism covering its local government, state and national offices to promote discipline and accountability among personnel. He also announced plans to move INEC staff from the conventional civil service salary structure to a special salary structure, which he said would take effect from January 1, 2027. According to him, the initiative is aimed at improving staff welfare and reducing the likelihood of electoral officials being induced before, during and after elections. “We want the new salary structure so that you will not easily be induced before, during and after election. We are working with other relevant governmental agencies and commissions to make the cash backing for the new salary structure possible,” he said. Amupitan urged staff to work diligently to restore and strengthen public confidence in the commission, stressing that their conduct was critical to the credibility of elections. “As an unbiased umpire, we need to improve the confidence and trust the people repose in us by being disciplined and diligent in the discharge of our duties at all times,” he said. In preparations for the forthcoming general election, the INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had provided its Enugu office with 10 new pickup vans, adding that more logistics would be made available. He said non-sensitive election materials were ready, while contracts for other required materials, including sensitive materials, were being processed. “Massive training and retraining will commence soon. The retraining is imperative, given the new guidelines and regulations introduced into the amended Electoral Act,” he added. item.content:encoded: …promises new salary structure By Chinedu Adonu The Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC), Prof. Joash Amupitan (SAN), has warned staff of the commission against partisan politics, urging them to maintain neutrality and professionalism in the discharge of their electoral duties. Amupitan gave the warning on Monday during an interactive session with INEC staff from the South-East region shortly after arriving in Enugu on a working visit to engage traditional rulers and electoral stakeholders in the zone. He said the commission would not tolerate unethical conduct or actions capable of undermining public confidence in the electoral process. “You should not pick interest in any political party. Be neutral and firm. I am hearing that some of you are showing interest in some political parties. This is absolutely wrong. “The commission wants you to be neutral and professional, both in your words and actions. The commission will not tolerate unprofessional or unethical electoral conduct from any staff,” he said. The INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had introduced a reward and sanction mechanism covering its local government, state and national offices to promote discipline and accountability among personnel. He also announced plans to move INEC staff from the conventional civil service salary structure to a special salary structure, which he said would take effect from January 1, 2027. According to him, the initiative is aimed at improving staff welfare and reducing the likelihood of electoral officials being induced before, during and after elections. “We want the new salary structure so that you will not easily be induced before, during and after election. We are working with other relevant governmental agencies and commissions to make the cash backing for the new salary structure possible,” he said. Amupitan urged staff to work diligently to restore and strengthen public confidence in the commission, stressing that their conduct was critical to the credibility of elections. “As an unbiased umpire, we need to improve the confidence and trust the people repose in us by being disciplined and diligent in the discharge of our duties at all times,” he said. In preparations for the forthcoming general election, the INEC chairman disclosed that the commission had provided its Enugu office with 10 new pickup vans, adding that more logistics would be made available. He said non-sensitive election materials were ready, while contracts for other required materials, including sensitive materials, were being processed. “Massive training and retraining will commence soon. item.title: Police smash suspected robbery gang, arrest six in Jigawa
item.description: ‎‎By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse ‎The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested six suspected members of an armed robbery gang responsible for attacks on residents of Jahun Local Government Area, during which cash, mobile phones and other valuables worth millions of naira were stolen. The command’s public relations officer, SP Lawan Shiisu Adam, disclosed this in a statement issued to journalists on Monday. ‎He said the arrests followed investigations into two armed robbery incidents reported in Jahun on September 24, 2026. ‎According to him, the gang invaded the residence of a 35-year-old man in Kofar Daru Quarters at about 2:00 a.m., making away with ₦20.18 million in cash, iTel mobile phones valued at ₦13.13 million, recharge cards worth ₦1 million, Android phones and other valuables. ‎He explained that the suspects also attacked the residence of a 37-year-old man in Shagari Quarters, where they stole ₦45,000, two blankets, rice and a woman’s wrapper. ‎Shiisu said detectives from Jahun Police Division immediately launched an investigation, which led to the arrest of five suspects. ‎He identified them as Sale Ibrahim, 25; Abubakar Abdullahi, 28; Babangida Ya’u, 35; Babannan Hassan, 27; and Isah Isibu, 35. ‎The police spokesperson said another breakthrough was recorded on October 15, 2026, when operatives of Maigatari Police Division, in collaboration with the Border Patrol Team, arrested a sixth suspect during a routine patrol at Maigatari Market. ‎The suspect identified as Isa Yusuf, 35, from Hantsu village in Miga Local Government Area, was found in possession of 13 new iTel mobile phones, 13 chargers, 13 batteries and ₦102,500 in cash. ‎He said the suspect was transferred to the State Criminal Investigation Department (SCID) in Dutse for further investigation. ‎According to Shiisu, the suspect confessed during interrogation to being a member of the gang involved in the Jahun robbery incidents. ‎He added that further investigation linked the recovered mobile phones and other items to the property stolen during the attacks. ‎The police spokesperson said all six suspects had been charged to court, while efforts were ongoing to track down other fleeing members of the gang and recover the remaining stolen property. ‎ The post Police smash suspected robbery gang, arrest six in Jigawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Anambra confirms Lassa fever case, activates emergency response
item.description: The Anambra Government has confirmed a Lassa fever case involving a patient linked to Omasi in Ayamelum Local Government Area (LGA), who is currently receiving treatment at the Federal Teaching Hospital, Abakaliki (FETHA), Ebonyi. The State Commissioner for Health, Dr Afam Obidike, disclosed this on Monday at an emergency stakeholders’ meeting in Awka. Obidike said the state had activated an emergency response to prevent further transmission. “The state has intensified disease surveillance and public awareness. “The meeting, attended by health partners, including the World Health Organisation and Médecins Sans Frontières, led to the activation of the Incident Management System. “Health officials will follow up on the affected household in Omasi, identify people who had contact with the patient and classify them according to their level of exposure for appropriate monitoring,” he said. The commissioner urged residents experiencing persistent fever or malaria-like symptoms that do not improve with appropriate treatment to seek medical attention promptly. He warned against relying solely on self-medication, stressing that early diagnosis and proper medical care were essential to managing the disease. Also speaking, the State Epidemiologist, Dr Chuma Emembolu, advised residents to keep food covered and store it in rodent-proof containers to prevent contamination by rats. Emembolu also urged residents to maintain clean surroundings and prevent rodents from contaminating food and household items with their urine and droppings. He further warned against direct contact with the blood and other body fluids of suspected or confirmed Lassa fever patients. The epidemiologist called for strict compliance with infection prevention measures and the guidance of health professionals. “We urge residents of Omasi and other communities in Ayamelum and the state at large to remain vigilant, cooperate with public health officials and avoid spreading unverified information. “These measures are aimed at strengthening preparedness, monitoring potential contacts and reducing the risk of further transmission,” he said. item.title: Tinubu’s reforms spare Nigeria deeper economic crisis – Shettima
item.description: Vice President Kashim Shettima says President Bola Tinubu’s economic decisions have spared Nigeria a deeper crisis that further delays in implementing critical reforms would have caused. Shettima said this on Monday while addressing leaders and members of the City Boy Movement at the State House Conference Hall in Abuja. He acknowledged the economic pressures Nigerians have endured, stressing that their sacrifices must translate into better livelihoods, more opportunities and improved living conditions. item.title: ‘My message twisted’ - Obi denies telling UK-based Nigerians to abandon loved ones
item.description: The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has denied asking Nigerians living in the United Kingdom to abandon relatives who depend on them for financial support, saying his message about hardship in Nigeria was distorted by political opponents. Obi said he appreciated Nigerians in the diaspora who made sacrifices to support their families at home, stressing that his concern was the country’s dependence on remittances to meet basic needs. In a statement titled “My Message Has Been Twisted”, posted on X on Tuesday, the former Anambra State governor said he never asked Nigerians abroad to stop supporting their loved ones. “I deeply appreciate Nigerians in the diaspora who work tirelessly and make enormous sacrifices to support their families back home,” he said. “Their remittances pay for school fees, hospital bills, rent, and feeding expenses. Their patriotism and sacrifices deserve our profound respect. I never asked them to abandon their loved ones.” Obi said his message was aimed at drawing attention to the economic conditions forcing millions of Nigerians to rely on relatives abroad for their survival. “My concern is that Nigeria should not remain a country where millions depend on relatives abroad for basic survival,” he said. “Our goal must be to build a nation that provides jobs, affordable healthcare, quality education, and economic opportunities for its citizens.” He accused political opponents of misrepresenting his comments, insisting that his position was about addressing the causes of hardship rather than discouraging financial assistance to families. “Political opponents may twist my message, but the truth remains clear: I am not asking Nigerians abroad to abandon their families. I am advocating for a Nigeria that will no longer abandon its own people,” he said. The clarification followed backlash over comments Obi made during a town hall meeting with diaspora supporters in Manchester on Sunday. In a video that went viral, Obi urged Nigerians in the UK to stop giving money to relatives and others at home who asked them for financial assistance, arguing that such support could ease hardship without addressing its underlying causes. “You have people at home in Nigeria today who are begging you for money. Tell them no!” he said. Obi attributed the country’s economic difficulties to poor leadership and urged Nigerians abroad to encourage their relatives and friends at home to vote for leaders who would prioritise productivity and economic opportunities. item.title: Fuel subsidy return could push Naira to N4,000/$ — Oyedele
item.description: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, has warned that a return to petrol subsidy could trigger capital flight, weaken investor confidence and push the naira to between N3,000 and N4,000 to the dollar. Oyedele gave the warning on Monday during a press briefing at the International Monetary Fund and World Bank Annual Meetings in Bangkok, Thailand. He said investors had repeatedly questioned whether the Federal Government would abandon its economic reforms ahead of the next election cycle. The minister ruled out reversing the reforms, warning that even a signal that President Bola Tinubu’s administration was considering reinstating petrol subsidy could unsettle financial markets, increase borrowing costs and worsen economic pressures on households. “In all the meetings I have had, I came to a conclusion that the markets, including the domestic market, which you can read from the capital market, and the international market, have largely written off the opposition in Nigeria as being unserious,” he said. Oyedele warned that any indication of a possible return to subsidy would trigger an immediate market reaction. “If, for any reason, the President were to say we are merely considering the return of fuel subsidy, capital would react immediately. “Airfares would struggle, the naira would come under severe pressure, potentially moving towards 3,000, 3,500 or even 4,000. The very fuel people want subsidised would become far more expensive in naira terms,” he stated. The minister added that capital flight could extend beyond foreign investors, as wealthy Nigerians, business owners and middle-class investors might also turn to the dollar as a hedge against uncertainty, further increasing demand for foreign exchange. Oyedele also rejected suggestions that the Nigerian National Petroleum Company Limited’s temporary reduction in petrol retail margins amounted to a return to subsidy. He explained that the reduction was a commercial decision rather than a payment funded by public resources, arguing that a company’s decision to lower its profit margin to make a product more affordable should not automatically be classified as a subsidy. item.title: National grid crashes 81% to 675MW, as 9 plants go off
item.description: By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Nigeria’s grid electricity supply crashed by 81.5 per cent to 675 megawatts (MW) at 1pm on Monday from 3,647MW, following a drop in the number of power plants supplying the national grid from 21 to 2. The development prompted electricity distribution companies, including Abuja Electricity Distribution Company (AEDC) and Ikeja Electric, to issue public notices informing customers of supply constraints linked to challenges on the national grid. Data from the Nigerian Independent System Operator (NISO) showed that 21 power plants were supplying electricity to the grid before the incident at noon, when total generation stood at 3,647MW. However, by 1pm, the number of plants on the grid had dropped to 12, while electricity supply plunged to 675MW, representing a loss of 2,972MW within one hour. The plants that went offline included Azura, Egbin, Jebba and Kainji hydroelectric power plants. The sharp decline followed relatively higher supply levels earlier in the day, with the grid recording 4,331MW at 1am and 4,458MW at 6am. Supply subsequently fell to 3,647MW by noon before experiencing the steep drop at 1pm. Electricity supply later recovered to 2,150MW by 5pm, representing an improvement of 1,475MW from the 1pm level, although it remained significantly below the morning peak. In a public notice issued on Monday, AEDC informed customers that electricity supply from the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) had been interrupted due to a grid-related challenge. The company said TCN’s technical team was working to restore grid stability, adding that power supply was gradually being restored to its feeders. “We assure you that efforts are ongoing to restore full supply across our franchise area as soon as the situation permits,” AEDC said, while apologising for the inconvenience caused by the interruption. Similarly, Ikeja Electric attributed reduced electricity supply across its network to a shortfall in the volume of power allocated to it from the national grid. In its notice to customers, the distribution company said it was engaging relevant stakeholders to improve available supply. It added that it would continue to distribute the electricity received from the grid as efficiently and equitably as possible. However, NISO said it had stabilised the national grid following multiple trippings on the 330-kilovolt (kV) transmission network. In a statement on Monday, the system operator said the incident occurred at approximately 12:40pm on October 19, 2026. It said it immediately implemented corrective measures in collaboration with TCN to stabilise the power system and restore normal operations. According to NISO, restoration efforts had been successfully completed and the national grid had returned to normal operation. The operator clarified that the incident affected only a section of the grid, contrary to unverified reports and claims. item.title: Customs reviews recruitment complaints, screens out 397 applicants
item.description: By Emma Ujah, Abuja Bureau Chief The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) has opened a fresh window for reviewing complaints from applicants disqualified during its recent recruitment exercise, following protests by some shortlisted candidates barred from proceeding to the training college. The Comptroller-General of Customs, Adewale Adeniyi, directed a case-by-case reassessment of the complaints after meeting with some of the aggrieved applicants. The NCS spokesperson, Abdullahi Maiwada, a Deputy Comptroller of Customs, disclosed this in a statement, saying the review was intended to ensure that legitimate grievances received appropriate attention. Adeniyi, however, warned that the exercise would not guarantee automatic admission, stressing that all affected candidates would undergo fresh screening and that anyone found to have engaged in certificate fraud or other criminal conduct would face prosecution. According to Maiwada, the recruitment process involves several stages of verification, including credential and document checks, physical fitness and endurance assessments, medical examinations, age verification and drug screening. item.title: NGX Group named Africa’s best Exchange at Euromoney Markets Awards 2026
item.description: By Providence Ayanfeoluwa & Glory Bassey Nigerian Exchange Group Plc (NGX Group) has been named Africa’s Best Exchange at the Euromoney Markets Awards 2026, recognising its contribution to market infrastructure, digital innovation and capital formation. Presented at the Mandarin Oriental Hyde Park, London, on Thursday, 15 October 2026, the award recognises achievements in market development during 2025 and comes amid robust growth in Nigeria’s equities market. A key driver of wider primary-market participation has been NGX Invest, the Group’s electronic public-offering platform, which simplifies subscriptions to public offers and rights issues. The platform played a significant role in Nigeria’s banking sector recapitalisation exercise, facilitating more than N2.8 trillion in capital raising. By September 2026, its distribution network had grown to more than 180 channels spanning stockbrokers, banks and fintechs, with a WhatsApp subscription channel providing investors with an additional channel for subscribing to public offers. Nigeria’s equities market recorded strong growth in 2025, with the NGX All-Share Index gaining 51.19 per cent, equities turnover rising 109.48 per cent to N5.96 trillion and market capitalisation reaching N99.38 trillion. This momentum has continued in 2026. As of 16 October, the All-Share Index had gained 59.07 per cent year-to-date. Equities turnover stood at N7.82 trillion, up 73.78 per cent from N4.50 trillion in the corresponding period of 2025, while market capitalisation reached N160.73 trillion. Temi Popoola, Group Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer of NGX Group, said: “This award reflects our continued commitment to strengthening the infrastructure and technology that support capital formation and investment. ‘‘We appreciate the trust and collaboration of our regulators, policymakers, issuers, investors, the stockbroking community and other market participants, whose support contributes to the development of our capital market. ‘‘By widening digital access to investment opportunities, improving market efficiency and deepening connections with other African markets, we are working to make our capital market more accessible, resilient and competitive.” ‘‘We see this not simply as an achievement, but as encouragement to keep building a market that can mobilise capital for businesses and offer broader investment opportunities.” Beyond digital innovation, NGX Group continues to advance sustainable finance through the NGX Net-Zero Programme (N-Zero), implemented in partnership with DEG Impulse gGmbH and Africa Foresight Group, with support through DEG Impulse’s develoPPP programme. The initiative helps Nigerian businesses strengthen climate readiness, establish science-based emissions-reduction targets and develop transition plans that can support access to climate-aligned finance. item.title: ‘APC has more problems within’ - Ndume affirms Shettima’s fear
item.description: Senator Ali Ndume, representing Borno South, has backed Vice President Kashim Shettima’s concern about internal divisions within the All Progressives Congress (APC), saying the ruling party faces more problems within its ranks than from the opposition. Ndume said opposition parties might be resilient and vocal ahead of the 2027 general elections, but argued that the struggle for power and the focus on personalities rather than ideas were more troubling. “I think the Vice President was just blunt. We have more problems within than without because, seeing that the opposition, quite alright, they are both resilient, tough and talking big, but it’s not the major problem,” the senator said. He added that politicians across party lines largely shared similar backgrounds, arguing that their differences were often driven by political platforms and the struggle for power. “That’s why they talk about personality instead of ideas, instead of events or debates on what to do and how to do it, and that’s dangerous,” Ndume said. The lawmaker accused politicians of taking Nigerians for granted, urging greater attention to policy debates and practical solutions to the country’s challenges. Ndume’s remarks followed Shettima’s recent warning that internal divisions within the APC posed a greater concern to the ruling party than its political opponents. The Vice President spoke on Saturday in Abuja at the unveiling of the campaign head office of Arewa for Asiwaju (A4A), a northern coalition supporting the Tinubu-Shettima ticket, where he also inaugurated the group’s campaign structure. “Honestly, I am not afraid of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP). I am not afraid of a diminished Peter Obi. But I am more afraid of internal contradictions within our household,” Shettima said. He maintained that unity within the ruling party would be crucial, adding, “If we unite as a people, as a family, we will conquer.” Shettima also warned northern political leaders against supporting Tinubu’s presidential campaign while undermining APC governors contesting at the state level. “There is no point in championing the cause of the presidential election and then undermining the governor in the gubernatorial election. Honestly, it will not go down well with the system,” he said. He urged party members to support APC governors, National Assembly members and Tinubu ahead of the next round of elections. “Let’s rally round our governors. Let’s rally round our members of the National Assembly. Let’s rally round President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and see to the victory in the next round of elections,” the Vice President added. I am not afraid of a diminished Peter Obi. But I am more afraid of internal contradictions within our household,” Shettima said. He maintained that unity within the ruling party would be crucial, adding, “If we unite as a people, as a family, we will conquer.” Shettima also warned northern political leaders against supporting Tinubu’s presidential campaign while undermining APC governors contesting at the state level. “There is no point in championing the cause of the presidential election and then undermining the governor in the gubernatorial election. Honestly, it will not go down well with the system,” he said. He urged party members to support APC governors, National Assembly members and Tinubu ahead of the next round of elections. “Let’s rally round our governors. Let’s rally round our members of the National Assembly. Let’s rally round President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and see to the victory in the next round of elections,” the Vice President added. Although the director of the department does not independently determine election results, the responsibilities attached to the office have drawn attention to the redeployment and calls for INEC to explain the considerations behind the decision. Adeyemi-Showunmi’s redeployment has sparked debate among civil society organisations and on social media over transparency, political neutrality and public confidence in the electoral body. Former director of voter education at INEC, Mr Nick Dazang, when contacted said, it would be wrong for the Commission to pretend that appointing someone that close to a sitting governor who is contesting elections has no implications. “The person may be eminently qualified but I have profound misgivings if he can discharge or execute his office as Resident Electoral Commissioner with the professionalism, neutrality and impartiality that the office demands. On the redeployment of Sowunmi wife, he said in the time past, and oblivious of the closeness/proximity of INEC officials to certain politically exposed persons, INEC officials on their merit, had been inadvertently assigned to roles/tasks that put them in difficult positions which complicated the Commission’s core values of impartiality and neutrality. He said In such circumstances, and in deference to its core values, INEC has demonstrated sensitivity by not posting such deserving officials to these positions. “It is likely that the Commission may not be aware or cognizant of the said officer’s relationship with a prominent politician. “But once this is established, and its attention is called to this reality, it should promptly do the needful, namely: not to put the officer in a position that compromises the Commission’s principles of neutrality and provision of a level playing field to all contestants. In the prevailing circumstance, the officer should be directed to recuse herself. This will allay fears, rightly or wrongly, that she has been procured to deliberately confer an advantage to any candidate(s) in the election. Either the tenure of the subsisting Director is specially extended for the period of the election, or his Deputy is directed to act in the position of Director, subject to consideration(s) of merit, federal character and the core values aforementioned,” he added. Director-General of YIAGA Africa, Samson Itodo, warned that the electoral body must ensure public confidence in the electoral process and should not take the people for granted in its appointment. On the appointment of Adeyemi-Showunmi as INEC Director of Electoral Operations, Itodo said elections are fundamentally about operations, adding that by this token, it is one of the most sensitive and consequential departments within INEC. He said, “In fact, the Electoral Operations Department is at the heart of election administration. From the recruitment and deployment of polling officials to the planning, production and distribution of election materials, as well as the operational arrangements for voting and results collation, the department plays a central role in determining how elections are conducted. “Mrs. Showunmi’s competence and professional capacity are not in doubt. However, competence alone is not sufficient for appointments to sensitive positions in election management. The independence, impartiality and perceived neutrality of those entrusted with managing elections are equally important. “Appointing individuals with strong ties to politicians in such strategic positions inevitably raises legitimate questions about impartiality and INEC independence. These concerns become even more pronounced in a climate of deep public distrust, growing fears of political capture of INEC, and politicians boldly declaring the number of votes they expect to secure before a single ballot has been cast. “At a time when public confidence in the electoral process is already fragile, appointments to critical positions within INEC should inspire confidence, not deepen suspicion. INEC must recognize that its credibility rests not only on the technical competence of its personnel but also on public confidence in INEC’s independence from partisan interests. Public confidence in the electoral process must never be taken for granted. In this instance, it is being taken for granted,” he said. Former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar was among those who first raised the alarm over the issue, demanding immediate and full transparency from INEC. In a statement issued by his Director of Strategic Communication, Phrank Shaibu, Atiku said the reported changes in the Electoral Operations Department raised serious questions that INEC must answer without delay. “Reports indicate that Director Isa Magaji Gummi was moved from Electoral Operations to the Voter Registry Department, while Mrs Oluyemi Titilayo Adeyemi-Showunmi was appointed to head Electoral Operations. Dr Lawrence Bayode has also been identified as the head of Information and Communication Technology (ICT). “These departments are at the heart of election administration. INEC must explain these decisions, publish the criteria applied and show that every appointment and redeployment followed due process, was based on merit and was free from political interference. Nigerians will not accept vague assurances on matters this serious.” Atiku said no official should be presumed compromised because of their ethnicity, background or associations. But when reported political connections or a concentration of appointments raises public concern, INEC must provide verifiable assurances that its impartiality is protected. “A government that has driven millions of Nigerians into hardship must not be allowed to turn the electoral umpire into an instrument of political survival. When sensitive election departments are reshaped and major contracts are surrounded by unanswered questions, the suspicion that a failing administration is seeking every possible advantage to cling to power will only grow. INEC must dispel that suspicion through full, immediate and verifiable disclosure,” he said.
